terms.gloss: there! (showing, or pointing to what has happened)
evidence: Plaut. Aul. 641: Em tibi, ostendī, eccās.
Plaut. Men. 625b: Em rūrsum nunc nūgās agis.
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: the same word as ēn, in the best manuscripts of Plautus and Terence (older editions print hem). With tibi, the flourish of “ta-da!”. For handing something over, see here you are.

terms.register: vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut.; Cic. in epistulīs
terms.comment: The vowel keeps the length of vidēs, as the house writes audīn’ from audīs.

evidence: Plaut. Men. 283: Dīxīn’ tibi esse hīc sȳcophantās plūrumōs?

phrases.latin: Ostende hūc manūs. — Em tibi, ostendī, eccās.
phrases.english: Show me your hands. — There, I’ve shown you: here they are.
There, now you’re talking nonsense again.

phrases.latin: sed vidēn’? fortūna hūmāna fingit artatque ut lubet
phrases.english: but do you see? fortune shapes and squeezes men as she likes

phrases.latin: Dīxīn’ tibi esse hīc sȳcophantās plūrumōs?
phrases.english: Didn’t I tell you there were plenty of tricksters here?
